html:
The Barghawata were a Berber tribal confederation that ruled the Atlantic plains of Morocco, the region called Tamesna between Salé and Safi, from 744 to 1058. They are shown here in 700.

They broke away from the Umayyad Caliphate in the Berber Revolt of the 740s. Their leader Salih ibn Tarif proclaimed himself a prophet and gave his followers a new faith, with a scripture in the Berber language, its own prayers and fasts, and food rules. Orthodox Muslim writers saw this as heresy.

The Barghawata held out against the Idrisids, the Umayyads of Córdoba and others for three centuries. The Almoravids finally destroyed them in the mid 11th century; the Almoravid founder, Abdallah ibn Yasin, was killed fighting them in 1059.
